findings.title: Double-checked locking is incomplete: cache is not re-checked after acquiring the write lock
findings.body: After the fast-path read-lock check fails, the function takes the exclusive write lock but never re-reads `entryPointAssetsCache`. During a cold start, every goroutine that got past the read-lock check (because the cache was still nil) will, one after another, acquire the write lock and re-open/parse `assets-manifest.json` even though the first one already populated the cache. Adding a `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }` check immediately after `Lock()` would make the initialization happen exactly once instead of once per concurrent request.

findings.title: Failed manifest read caches nil and now serializes every request on the write mutex
findings.body: When `readWebAssetsFromFile` fails, `result` is nil and `entryPointAssetsCache = result` stores nil, so the fast path never short-circuits. Previously these repeated retries were lock-free; now every single request that renders the index page must take the exclusive `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` and perform a failing `os.Open`/JSON decode while holding it. A missing or malformed `assets-manifest.json` therefore turns into a global serialization point (all HTTP handlers queueing on one mutex plus disk I/O), which is far worse than a plain error. Consider only overwriting the cache when `result != nil` (and/or caching the failure with a backoff).

findings.title: Blocking network I/O performed while holding the global write lock
findings.body: `readWebAssetsFromCDN` issues an HTTP GET with `http.DefaultClient` (no explicit timeout) while `entryPointAssetsCacheMu` is held exclusively. If the CDN path is ever enabled (the `cdn` variable is currently hardcoded to ""), a slow or hanging CDN would block every other caller of `GetWebAssets` for the duration of the request, since readers also need the same mutex. The I/O should be done outside the lock, with the lock only taken to publish the result.

findings.title: No test covers the concurrent access that this PR fixes
findings.body: The PR is a race-condition fix but adds no test. A small test that calls `GetWebAssets` from several goroutines concurrently (both with `cfg.Env == setting.Dev`, which always rewrites the cache, and with the production env) would fail under `-race` before the change and pass after, preventing a future regression when the `// TODO: get rid of global state` cleanup happens.
